headline: Restricted Nvidia chips surface at a China data center
dek: According to Bloomberg, cited by Engadget and Tecmundo, loan documents tie the hardware to Shanghai.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: What the documents show
body: A Shanghai data center allegedly housed Blackwell chips, which need a US license to go to China (Engadget, Tecmundo).
A rack was pledged as loan collateral, per Bloomberg as cited by Engadget.

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: The equipment
s3.body: The site is the Yangtze River Delta Project, a supercomputing complex.

points.t: One GB300 NVL72 packs Blackwell Ultra GPUs and Grace processors (Engadget).
Shanghai Shuoyao pledged the rack for a loan (Tecmundo).
Bloomberg also found Hopper-generation servers on site (Engadget).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why it matters
body: The US is probing whether Megaspeed broke export rules, which it denies (Engadget).
Neither outlet explains how the chips reached China (Engadget, Tecmundo).

items.t: Jensen Huang testifies before the US Senate on December 3 (Engadget).
A rack serial number led to Gigabyte (Engadget).
Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment (Engadget).

caption.hook: Restricted Nvidia chips appear at a data center in China, according to documents cited by Bloomberg.
body: According to Engadget and Tecmundo, Shanghai Shuoyao pledged a GB300 rack as collateral for a loan of about $14 million. The hardware was allegedly installed at a supercomputing complex in Shanghai, where Bloomberg also found Hopper-generation servers.

The US Justice Department is investigating whether Megaspeed violated export rules, and the company denies wrongdoing (Engadget). Neither outlet explains how the chips reached China. Gigabyte said it follows the law, and Nvidia did not comment. The full story is at the link in bio.
caption.cta: Can export controls on AI chips work if the hardware moves through resellers?
